code.originalText: Two-week heart failure medication safety check and echocardiogram

text.paragraph: Two-week heart failure medication safety check, echocardiogram, and cardiology review. [S]

Mr. Roosevelt returns two weeks after starting sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol, empagliflozin, and furosemide for newly diagnosed heart failure. He is less breathless: he now propels his wheelchair the length of a long corridor before he has to rest, and he sleeps on two pillows without waking breathless. His leg swelling is less by evening. His home weights on a wheelchair scale have fallen by about 3 kg, and his home blood pressures run in the 140s over 80s. He has had no lightheadedness on transfers, no lip or tongue swelling, and no genital itching or urinary symptoms, and he has taken every dose. He still tires by late afternoon. He stopped smoking on his quit date last week and wears the nicotine patch every day; cravings come mostly in long meetings. He has had no muscle aches on atorvastatin. His echocardiogram and cardiology consultation were done this morning. [S]

value.displayName: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure

list.item:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, improving (I50.22). Echocardiography today shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30 percent, confirming heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. He is better but still mildly congested (jugular venous pressure 9 cm, basal crackles, 1+ edema); NYHA class II to III. After two weeks of sacubitril/valsartan, empagliflozin, and furosemide, potassium is 4.8 mmol/L and creatinine 1.29 mg/dL (eGFR 63), a 9 percent rise that is well within the 30 percent accepted when this therapy starts. [S]
Increase sacubitril/valsartan to 49/51 mg twice daily.
Increase carvedilol to 6.25 mg twice daily with food.
Start spironolactone 25 mg daily: potassium is below 5.0 mmol/L and eGFR above 30.
Continue empagliflozin 10 mg daily and furosemide 20 mg daily.
Basic metabolic panel in one to two weeks, drawn at the second iron infusion, because sacubitril/valsartan rises and spironolactone starts today.
Cardiology agrees with the titration plan; repeat echocardiogram three to six months after tolerated doses are reached.

Iron deficiency in heart failure (D50.9). Ferritin 48 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 16 percent at diagnosis, with hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL. This meets the heart failure criteria for intravenous iron, which improves symptoms and exercise capacity. [S]
Ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg intravenously today and again in one week.
Recheck hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation at the three-month review.

Hypertensive heart disease (I11.0). Blood pressure 148/88 mmHg, down from 186/108 at diagnosis but above the 130/80 target; home readings agree. [S]
Today's increases in sacubitril/valsartan and carvedilol and the new spironolactone are expected to lower it.
Continue the home blood pressure and daily weight log and the low-sodium diet.

Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, newly abstinent (F17.210). No cigarettes since his quit date last week, on a 21 mg nicotine patch. [S]
Continue the patch daily.
Plan for meeting cravings reviewed: leave the room briefly, and keep his hands busy.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). Atorvastatin 40 mg started two weeks ago for LDL cholesterol 132 mg/dL; no muscle symptoms. [S]
Lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks after the start, to confirm the response.
